description: A fail-closed evaluation rubric specification for cloud/GPU workloads and ROS 2 robotics configurations. It does not itself run Gazebo, NVIDIA Isaac Sim, GPU fault injection, hardware tests, or safety certification.

scoring_axes.threshold_notice: The numeric velocity thresholds are sample screening defaults only. They must be replaced or approved for the exact robot, payload, operating mode, manufacturer limits, and lab safety case.

scoring_axes.network_notice: Distributed ROS 2 may require an explicitly approved isolated interface; do not force loopback without validating the deployment topology.

scoring_axes.gpu_notice: GPU utilization, idle ratio, MIG partition state, and resource limits require telemetry or semantic inspection; text-pattern scanning alone cannot prove them.

receipt_integrity.hash_scope: exact UTF-8 bytes of the submitted preflight manifest, without newline or whitespace normalization
receipt_integrity.signature_and_key_custody: A SHA-256 digest detects byte changes but does not authenticate the issuer. A production digital signature requires managed signing keys, key custody, rotation, and verification.

currently_available: Cloudflare Worker fingerprints the submitted /api/preflight manifest and stores its SHA-256 digest in the receipt.
An authenticated verification endpoint compares the exact submitted manifest bytes against the stored digest and blocks on mismatch.
The verifier fails closed unless a simulation attestation and explicit human sign-off are present.
not_yet_available: Gazebo or NVIDIA Isaac Sim physics integration
Physical robot or NVIDIA Jetson boot enforcement
Trusted simulator attestation issuance and signing
Robot actuator, emergency-stop, geofence, torque, and battery safety enforcement
GPU telemetry-backed idle-ratio or MIG verification
implementation_disclosure.safety_notice: The current ROS 2 CI messaging smoke test is not a physics simulation. The Worker verification endpoint is not itself an admission controller and does not stop a device from booting. A separately installed cluster admission controller or edge agent must enforce the verification decision.
